regional_nuance.tone: Warm, conversational, and relationship-first. Mexican business culture values trust ('confianza') and personal connection before the transaction. Avoid overly formal Castilian Spanish — prefer the inclusive 'ustedes' over 'vosotros', and lean into approachable directness rather than stiff corporate language.
cultural_values: pride in Mexican identity and craftsmanship
taboos: Avoid comparisons that imply Mexican products are inferior to US/European ones
Do not use Castilian vosotros constructs
Avoid overly legalistic or cold tone — it reads as distrust
motivators: Value and 'buen precio' (good deal) without feeling cheap
Aspirational imagery tied to family success

slang_and_idioms.meaning: Expression of agreement, encouragement, or approval — 'Let's go!' / 'Exactly!'

slang_and_idioms.usage: Problem-acknowledgment copy before presenting the solution
Reacting to a product reveal or feature highlight

slang_and_idioms.meaning: Step on it / Go for it
slang_and_idioms.usage: Action-oriented CTAs for sales or sign-up flows
Speed/efficiency messaging for B2B only, informal contexts

seo_behavior.keyword_style: Users search in full conversational phrases and questions more than keyword fragments. Include long-tail question-format keywords.
seo_behavior.local_signals: Include 'en México', city names (CDMX, Guadalajara, Monterrey), and 'envío a domicilio' / 'disponible en México' for e-commerce
seo_behavior.meta_title_style: Lead with the primary benefit, include 'México' or city for local intent, keep under 60 characters
seo_behavior.meta_description_style: Conversational, include a clear action phrase ('Cotiza gratis', 'Envío gratis'), 150–160 characters
seo_behavior.content_length_preference: Mid-form (600–900 words) with clear H2/H3 structure performs best; listicles and how-to guides rank well

formatting.currency: MXN — display as '$' prefix or 'MXN' suffix (e.g., $1,299 MXN)
formatting.number_separators: Period for thousands, comma for decimals (e.g., 1.299,50) — note: some regions use comma for thousands, validate per context
formatting.punctuation_style: Use inverted question mark (¿) and exclamation mark (¡) at sentence start
formatting.address_order: Street name + number, Colonia, City, State, CP (Postal Code), México
formatting.formal_register: Use 'usted' for B2B and older audiences; 'tú' for B2C, youth, and lifestyle brands

regional_nuance.tone: Precise, factual, and credibility-driven. German consumers and business audiences are highly skeptical of hyperbole — they expect claims to be substantiated. Lead with specifications, certifications, and concrete outcomes rather than emotional appeals. Directness is a sign of respect, not rudeness.
cultural_values: Engineering excellence ('Made in Germany' halo effect
taboos: Avoid superlatives without proof ('best', 'leading') — they read as dishonest
Never downplay data privacy or skip GDPR-compliance signals
Avoid casual or overly familiar tone in B2B contexts
Exaggerated emotional language feels manipulative
motivators: Third-party certifications and test results (Stiftung Warentest, TÜV)

slang_and_idioms.meaning: All good / Got it — acknowledgment of clarity
So what? — used rhetorically to challenge the status quo
slang_and_idioms.usage: Problem-framing copy: 'Na und, was bringt das wirklich?'
Feature reveal copy for highly engaged audiences
Value-proposition copy emphasizing simplicity and directness

slang_and_idioms.meaning: Things are going well for you — often ironic

slang_and_idioms.usage: Brand copy that leans into precision and reliability

slang_and_idioms.meaning: Put to the test (lit. test on heart and kidneys)

seo_behavior.search_engine: Google.de dominates (~90%); Bing has minor share
seo_behavior.keyword_style: German compound nouns are dominant search terms — users combine words into long single-word queries (e.g., 'Projektmanagementsoftware', 'Buchhaltungssoftware'). Always target compound variants alongside spaced versions.
seo_behavior.local_signals: Include 'Deutschland', 'deutschlandweit', city names (Berlin, München, Hamburg) for local intent. DSGVO-compliant signals improve trust and may influence CTR.
seo_behavior.meta_title_style: Factual benefit + key noun, include brand name at end, 55–60 characters. Avoid clickbait.
seo_behavior.meta_description_style: Factual, include specific numbers or proof points, clear action verb, 150–160 characters
seo_behavior.content_length_preference: Long-form (1,200–2,000 words) with thorough coverage performs best — thin content is trusted less; include technical depth, comparisons, and citations where possible

formatting.currency: EUR — display as '€' prefix or suffix per context (e.g., 1.299,00 €)
formatting.number_separators: Period for thousands, comma for decimals (e.g., 1.299,50)
formatting.punctuation_style: Standard German — use „Anführungszeichen” (lower-9 opening, upper-6 closing) for quotations
formatting.address_order: Street name + number, Postleitzahl (PLZ) City, Deutschland
formatting.formal_register: Always use 'Sie' (formal you) in B2B and for unknown audiences; 'du' only in explicitly casual B2C brands targeting youth

regional_nuance.tone: Sophisticated, precise, and intellectually confident. French audiences respond to craft, elegance, and substance — copy should feel considered and well-written, never rushed or breathless. Avoid aggressive sales tactics or hyperbole; instead, let the quality of the product and the clarity of the argument do the work. Wit and a light touch of irony are welcome in B2C contexts.
taboos: Avoid loud, hard-sell Americanisms — 'AMAZING DEAL!!!' reads as vulgar
Never underestimate the audience's intelligence or over-explain the obvious
Avoid anglicisms unless the brand deliberately uses them for a modern/tech feel
Do not use 'tu' in formal or unknown contexts — 'vous' is the safe default
motivators: Clarity of argument — French audiences want to be convinced, not manipulated
Environmental and ethical responsibility (especially among under-35s)

slang_and_idioms.usage: Casual product highlight copy for B2C
Results and outcome copy: 'Faites un carton plein avec votre campagne'
Emphasis in B2C lifestyle copy: 'hyper efficace', 'hyper simple'

slang_and_idioms.meaning: It's in the bag / it's a done deal
Something you fall in love with at first sight

seo_behavior.search_engine: Google.fr dominates (>92% share); Bing and Qwant have minor shares
seo_behavior.keyword_style: French users search with full phrases and often include prepositions and articles ('le meilleur logiciel de…', 'comment faire…'). Keyword stuffing reads as unnatural — prioritise semantic richness and natural phrasing.
seo_behavior.local_signals: Include 'en France', 'pour les entreprises françaises', city names (Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Bordeaux) for local SEO. 'Livraison en France' and 'service client français' are strong trust signals.
seo_behavior.meta_title_style: Factual and benefit-led; include a relevant keyword naturally; brand name at end separated by '|'; 55–60 characters. Avoid exclamation marks in titles.
seo_behavior.meta_description_style: Elegant and informative; include a concrete proof point or benefit; clear but non-aggressive action phrase ('Découvrez', 'Essayez gratuitement'); 150–160 characters
seo_behavior.content_length_preference: Long-form (1,000–1,500 words) with well-structured argumentation performs best; listicles work but should feel substantive rather than superficial; 'Guides complets' and 'Dossiers' outperform shallow how-tos

formatting.currency: EUR — display as '€' suffix with non-breaking space (e.g., 1 299,00 €). Never prefix.
formatting.number_separators: Non-breaking space for thousands, comma for decimals (e.g., 1 299,50)
formatting.punctuation_style: Standard French — use « guillemets » (angle quotes) for quotations. Add a non-breaking space before : ; ! ? — e.g., 'Résultat : 42 %'
formatting.address_order: Number + Street name, Postal code City, France (e.g., 12 rue de la Paix, 75001 Paris, France)
formatting.formal_register: Always use 'vous' in B2B and for unknown audiences; 'tu' only in explicitly youth-facing or casual B2C brands. Avoid overly familiar tone unless the brand identity demands it.

regional_nuance.tone: Energetic, warm, and optimistic. Brazilians respond strongly to enthusiasm, humor, and a sense of possibility ('o Brasil que dá certo'). Copy should feel like a conversation with a knowledgeable friend, not a corporate announcement. Storytelling and emotion drive decisions more than specs alone.
cultural_values: Community and togetherness ('juntos somos mais fortes')
taboos: Avoid European Portuguese (Portugal) constructs — they sound foreign and stiff to Brazilians
Don't be overly formal unless the context demands it (legal, financial)
Avoid pessimistic or fear-based framing — Brazilians respond better to aspiration
Do not conflate Brazil with other Latin American countries
motivators: Social proof and community validation ('todo mundo já está usando')

slang_and_idioms.meaning: To kill it / To absolutely excel
It's on / Let's go (very current slang)
slang_and_idioms.usage: Launch announcements, campaign kickoffs — use for younger demographics

slang_and_idioms.meaning: Go for it / Give it your all
Split into installments — extremely important in Brazilian e-commerce
slang_and_idioms.usage: Always mention installment options in pricing copy: 'em 12x de R$X'

seo_behavior.keyword_style: Brazilians search in natural spoken language — long conversational queries are common. Voice search is growing fast (high mobile penetration). Include question-format and colloquial variants.
seo_behavior.local_signals: Include 'no Brasil', 'para brasileiros', state/city names (São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, etc.), and 'frete grátis' / 'entrega rápida' for e-commerce. Regional targeting (Sudeste, Nordeste) can be powerful for physical products.
seo_behavior.meta_title_style: Benefit-first, conversational, include 'no Brasil' or city for local intent, 55–60 characters
seo_behavior.meta_description_style: Energetic, include social proof signal or urgency, clear action verb, 150–160 characters
seo_behavior.content_length_preference: Mid-form (700–1,100 words) with scannable structure; video and visual content outperforms pure text — embed or reference video where possible; listicles with numbered steps perform exceptionally well

formatting.currency: BRL — display as 'R$' prefix (e.g., R$ 1.299,90). Always offer installment framing: 'ou 12x de R$ 108,32'
formatting.number_separators: Period for thousands, comma for decimals (e.g., 1.299,90)
formatting.punctuation_style: Standard Portuguese — use ”aspas” or standard double quotes; avoid curly quotes in digital copy
formatting.address_order: Street type + name + number, Complemento, Bairro, City – State abbreviation, CEP XXXXX-XXX, Brasil
formatting.formal_register: Use 'você' universally (both B2B and B2C) — 'tu' is regional (South/Northeast Brazil); avoid 'vós' entirely

regional_nuance.tone: Warm, energetic, and conversational Nigerian English. Nigeria is linguistically diverse (English is the lingua franca across Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa and hundreds of other languages), so write in clear, standard Nigerian English and do NOT assume a single dialect or slang register. This profile serves both local Nigerian audiences and the international/diaspora audience — default to English that works for both, and localise slang only for brands that clearly target a local youth audience. Be respectful of elders, titles and faith; keep commercial messaging direct, confident and upbeat ('can-do' hustle energy) without being aggressive.
cultural_values: community and extended family ('we rise by lifting others')
hustle, ambition and entrepreneurship ('hustle' is positive)
respect for elders, titles and authority
faith and optimism (reference respectfully, never flippantly)
pride in Nigerian identity and 'Naija' creativity
taboos: Do not assume all Nigerians use Pidgin or any single slang register — default to clear standard Nigerian English
Avoid negative stereotypes about any ethnic group, region or religion
Do not mock or overuse religious language — keep it respectful and optional
Avoid condescending 'Western saviour' framing — position the audience as capable and ambitious
Do not invent Naira prices, revenue or follower counts — only convert/state what the source actually says
motivators: value for money and trustworthiness (fraud is a real concern — prove legitimacy)
belonging to community and social proof

slang_and_idioms.meaning: Colloquial, affectionate name for Nigeria / Nigerian
slang_and_idioms.usage: Brand identity and pride moments (optional, not forced)
Optional — only for youth-focused brands, never general B2B

seo_behavior.search_engine: Google.com.ng dominates, with strong Google (general) and social discovery (Instagram, TikTok, WhatsApp) for Nigerian users
seo_behavior.keyword_style: Nigerian users search in full conversational phrases, often adding 'in Nigeria', city names (Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, Ibadan), 'price', and 'how to'. Include long-tail question keywords and local place names.
seo_behavior.local_signals: Reference NGN pricing, Lagos/Abuja/Port Harcourt, 'nationwide delivery', 'Pay on delivery' where relevant, and trust signals (verified, secure payment) for legitimacy
seo_behavior.meta_title_style: Lead with the benefit, include 'Nigeria' or a city for local intent, keep under 60 characters
seo_behavior.meta_description_style: Conversational, include a clear action and a trust signal ('Nationwide delivery', 'Pay on delivery'), 150–160 characters
seo_behavior.content_length_preference: Mid-form (600–900 words) with clear H2/H3 structure; how-to guides, listicles and price-focused content perform well

formatting.time_format: Africa/Lagos (WAT, UTC+1, no DST). 12-hour with AM/PM for consumer copy (e.g., 3:00 PM WAT); 24-hour for logistics/B2B.
formatting.currency: NGN (Nigerian Naira) — format as ₦ with comma thousands and no decimals unless needed (e.g., ₦1,299). Convert any USD references to ₦ with an approximate rate (~₦1,500 = $1 USD) and flag with '(aprox.)'.
formatting.number_separators: Comma for thousands, period for decimals (e.g., 1,299.50)
formatting.punctuation_style: Standard English punctuation; exclamation marks are acceptable for excitement but do not overuse
formatting.address_order: House number + street, area, city, state, Nigeria
formatting.formal_register: Respectful but approachable; 'you' is fine for most B2C. For B2B and older audiences use full sentences and titles (Mr/Mrs/Dr) where appropriate.

regional_nuance.tone: Warm, expressive, conversational Nigerian Pidgin (Naijá). Pidgin is informal and spoken-first, so write the way people actually talk, with natural rhythm and short clauses. Keep it broadly intelligible (avoid niche slang that only one city/age group knows). Use Pidgin for consumer/youth brands and the spoken voice layer; for formal B2B or older audiences default to standard Nigerian English (en-NG). Never claim natural spoken-Pidgin delivery is verified without fluent-speaker review.
cultural_values: community and extended family ('we dey carry each other')
respect for elders, titles and authority
pride in Naija identity and creativity
taboos: Do not claim natural spoken-Pidgin audio is verified - written Pidgin only, until fluent-speaker review
Do not overuse slang that excludes older or non-youth audiences
Avoid negative stereotypes about any ethnic group, region or religion
Keep any prices/claims factual - convert to ₦ with 'aprox.' where the source is USD
Do not mock or overuse religious language
motivators: value for money and trustworthiness (fraud is a real concern — prove legitimacy)
belonging to community and social proof
